title: Does Real Estate Lead the Business Cycle in Vietnam? Evidence from Quarterly Data
content: This study examines the cyclical relationship between real estate activity and broader macroeconomic growth in Vietnam, with particular attention to structural stability during the 2022-2023 financial stress episode and the predictive role of real estate developments. Using an audited quarterly dataset covering 2011Q2-2026Q1, the analysis constructs GDP excluding real estate value added to minimise mechanical accounting overlap. Ordinary least squares estimation with heteroskedasticity- and autocorrelation-consistent standard errors, a Chow structural-break test, and bidirectional Granger-causality tests are employed. The results reveal a strong positive association between real estate value-added growth and broader economic activity (β = 1.075, p < 0.001), although statistically significant more-than-proportional sensitivity is not established. Real estate activity also exhibits relatively favourable conditional performance during the COVID-19 period. No statistically significant structural break is detected around the 2022-2023 financial stress episode, although the limited post-break sample constrains inference. Granger-causality tests indicate that real estate activity provides predictive information about subsequent macroeconomic growth, while evidence of reverse predictive relationships suggests bidirectional dynamics. These findings highlight the potential value of real estate indicators for macroeconomic monitoring and financial stability assessment in Vietnam. However, unresolved stationarity concerns and limited quarterly credit data restrict causal interpretation and the identification of financial transmission mechanisms.
